div.l: Well cowde he kepe a garner ⁊and a bynne
Ther was non auditour coude of hym wynne
Well wyst he by the droughte ⁊and by the rayn
The yeldynge of his sede ⁊and of his grayn
His lordis shepe his neet and his deyrie
His swyne his hors his store ⁊and his pultrye
Was hooly in this reuys gouernyng
And by his couenaunt yaf the rekenyng
Syth his lorde was twenty yere of aege
Ther cowde noman brynge hym in arerage
Ther nas baylly ne none other hyne
That he ne knewe his sleyghte or his couyne
They were of hym adrad as of the deth
His dwellyng was full fayr vpon an heth
Wyth grene trees shadowed was his place
He cowde better than his lorde purchace
Full ryche he was astoryd pryuely
His lorde well he cowde pleace subtylly
To yeue and lene to hym of his owne good
And haue thank and yet a cote ⁊and an hood
In youthe he had lerned a good mystere
He was a wel good wryght a carpentere
This reue sat vpon a wel good stot
That was all pomell grey ⁊and lyght scot
A long surcote vpon hym he hadde
And by his syde he bare a rusty bladde
Of northfolk was this reue of whyche I telle
Besyde a towne men calle baldeswelle
Tuckyd he was as is a frere abowte
And euer he rode the hynderest of the rowte
Sompnour wyth vs was in that place
That had a fyre redde cherubyns face
For sausfleme he was wyth eyen narow
Hote he was and lykorous as a sparow
Wyth blak browes skallyd ⁊and pylled berde
Of his vysage chyldren wrre a ferde
Ther nas quyksylner lytarge ne brymstone
Borace ceruse ne oyle of tarter none
Ne oynement that wolde clense ⁊and byte
That hym myght helpe of his whelkis whyte
